evidence.quote: SR-1 — Append-only collections (`completions`, `streak_events`, `learning_ledger`, `points_ledger`) deny value mutation on update: allow only idempotent identical replay.

finding.why: Confirmed by grep: no `resource.data == request.resource.data`-style identical-replay guard exists anywhere in firestore.rules (447 lines, zero hits). Every SR-1-named collection's update branch is just `isOwner(uid)` (plus unrelated format checks on completions only) — an owner-authenticated client (a modified build, a compromised device, or a bug in the sync engine's outbox-retry logic) can silently overwrite an EXISTING completion's points, a streak event, or a ledger/points-ledger entry with any new value, and the rule accepts it as an ordinary update. firestore_rules.test.mjs is this repo's only server-side gate test for owner writes and its own header claims it 'locks the LOAD-BEARING security boundaries' — yet none of its 4 SR-1 describe blocks (completions:306, streak_events:337, learning_ledger:347, points_ledger:357) ever attempt a changed-value update and assert it fails; each only proves identical-value re-writes and tutor-writes are handled. This is exactly the risk coding-standards.md itself names for SR-1: 'a child's study record is tamperable' — and since points/streak/ledger entries feed reward_redemptions (real-world reward fulfilment), undetected mutation directly undermines the rewards economy's integrity, with zero test coverage to catch a regression today or after any future fix.
finding.recommendation: For each of completions/streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger, add a test that seeds a doc then attempts an owner update with a changed field value and asserts it fails; pair with a firestore.rules change adding `request.resource.data == resource.data` as an allowed alternative to full validation on update.
acceptance_criteria: firestore_rules.test.mjs adds one assertFails case per SR-1 collection where an owner updates an existing doc with a changed field value
`make test-rules` fails against today's firestore.rules and passes once firestore.rules adds an identical-replay branch for each SR-1 collection
